english: Let $S$ be the set of all complex numbers $z$ satisfying $|z-4-2i|=2$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$. Then the minimum value of $\mathrm{Re}\left(\dfrac{\bar{z}}{z}\right)+\mathrm{Im}\left(\dfrac{\bar{z}}{z}\right)$ over $z\in S$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $S$ उन सभी सम्मिश्र संख्याओं $z$ का समुच्चय है जो $|z-4-2i|=2$ को संतुष्ट करती हैं, जहाँ $i=\sqrt{-1}$ है। तब $z\in S$ पर $\mathrm{Re}\left(\dfrac{\bar{z}}{z}\right)+\mathrm{Im}\left(\dfrac{\bar{z}}{z}\right)$ का न्यूनतम मान ______ है।
solution: Circle: centre $4+2i$, radius $2$, touches the real axis at $4$; $0\notin S$. Let $\phi=\arg(4+2i)$, $\tan\phi=\dfrac{1}{2}$; tangents from $O$ make angles $0$ and $2\phi$, so $\theta\in[0,2\phi]$
$\cos4\phi=-\dfrac{7}{25}>-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, so $4\phi<\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$; then $2\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\in\left[\dfrac{\pi}{4},\pi\right)$, where the cosine is decreasing
solution_full: So the expression equals $\cos2\theta-\sin2\theta=\sqrt{2}\cos\left(2\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$; it depends only on $\arg z$.
The circle has centre $4+2i$ and radius $2$; its distance from the real axis is $2$, so it touches the real axis at $z=4$. The origin is outside ($|4+2i|=2\sqrt{5}>2$), so $z\neq0$ on $S$.

Let $\phi=\arg(4+2i)$, so $\tan\phi=\dfrac{1}{2}$. The two tangents from the origin are symmetric about the line through the centre; one is the real axis (angle $0$), so the other makes angle $2\phi$. Hence $\arg z$ takes every value in $[0,2\phi]$ on $S$.

Since $\cos4\phi=-\dfrac{7}{25}>-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ and both angles lie in $(0,\pi)$, $4\phi<\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$. Hence for $t\in[0,4\phi]$, $t+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\in\left[\dfrac{\pi}{4},\pi\right)$, where $\cos$ is decreasing; so the least value occurs at $t=4\phi$, the largest argument.
Minimum at $t=4\phi$: $\cos4\phi-\sin4\phi=-\dfrac{7}{25}-\dfrac{24}{25}=-\dfrac{31}{25}=-1.24$, attained at the point of contact $z=\dfrac{12+16i}{5}$ of the second tangent.
originality_note: New: zbar/z = e^{-2i theta} turns the expression into a function of arg z, and the range of arg z on a circle touching the real axis is [0, 2 phi] by the tangent symmetry, so the extremum sits at a tangent point (way 5). Closest known: greatest argument of z on a circle. Different because: the quantity is a trigonometric function of 2 arg z, so its extremum needs the double angle of the tangent angle and a monotonicity check.

concept_use.Conjugate, modulus and argument of a com: zbar/z has modulus 1 and argument -2 arg z; the range of arg z on the circle comes from the tangents through the origin.
concept_use.Polar form and exponential form of compl: z = r e^{i theta} gives zbar/z = e^{-2i theta}, so Re + Im = cos 2theta - sin 2theta.

key_step: Reduce to cos 2theta - sin 2theta, find the argument range [0, 2phi] of the circle from the tangent symmetry, and evaluate at the end point.
justification: Two linked ideas (exponential form of zbar/z, argument range of a circle) with double-angle work and a monotonicity check, no options. Average Advanced numerical, like 2023-P1-Q11 (L3).
